summary: This Wikipedia-derived note covers several aspects of the 2008 Sichuan earthquake: a claimed earthquake prediction by former China Seismological Bureau researcher Geng Qingguo and official denial, seismologists' explanations of the quake's severity and duration, engineering criticism of older building codes, the fate of pandas at the Wolong reserve, and the operation to drain a dangerous quake lake at Mount Tangjia. It also notes large donations from state-owned enterprises.
one_line: Overview of the 2008 Sichuan earthquake covering disputed prediction claims, seismology, building damage, panda reserve impacts, and quake-lake relief.
key_facts: Former China Seismological Bureau researcher Geng Qingguo claimed a confidential report was sent to the State Seismological Bureau on April 30, 2008, warning of a significant earthquake in Ngawa Prefecture around May 8.
Geng Qingguo believed that "the bigger the earthquake, the easier it is to predict."
Geng Qingguo's drought-earthquake correlation theory was first released in 1972 and was said to have predicted the 1975 Haicheng and 1976 Tangshan earthquakes.

An official with the Seismological Bureau said that "earthquake prediction is widely acknowledged around the world to be difficult from a scientific standpoint" and denied receiving reports predicting the earthquake.
Yuji Yagi of the University of Tsukuba said the earthquake occurred in two stages, with the 155-mile Longmenshan Fault tearing in two sections.
Yuji Yagi's data showed the earthquake lasted about two minutes and released 30 times the energy of the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake in Japan, which killed over 6,000 people.
Teruyuki Kato of the University of Tokyo said seismic waves traveled a long distance without losing power because of the firmness of the terrain in central China.
Reginald DesRoches of Georgia Tech said massive building damage occurred because China did not create an adequate seismic design code until after the 1976 Tangshan earthquake.
Officials initially could not contact the Wolong National Nature Reserve, home to around 280 giant pandas.
A group of 31 British tourists visiting the Wolong Panda Reserve returned safe and uninjured to Chengdu, according to the Foreign Ministry.
Five security guards at the Wolong reserve were killed by the earthquake, and six pandas escaped after their enclosures were damaged.
By May 28, 2008, one panda was still missing; it was later found dead under the rubble of an enclosure.
Nine-year-old Mao Mao, a mother of five at the breeding center, was killed when a wall crushed her enclosure.

The quake lake at Mount Tangjia in Beichuan County was accessible only by foot or air, and an Mi-26T heavy lift helicopter of China Flying Dragon Special Aviation Company brought in heavy earthmoving tractors.
More than 200,000 people were evacuated from Mianyang by June 1 in anticipation of the dam bursting.
China National Petroleum Corp and Sinopec each donated 10 million yuan to the disaster area, and central state-owned enterprises accumulatively donated more than $48.6 million.
